articles.title: DeepSeek, Alibaba among major Chinese AI firms accused of stealing trade secrets of American counterparts
articles.summary: US News: The United States on Tuesday accused Chinese Artificial Intelligence firms, including DeepSeek and Alibaba, of stealing trade secrets of their America.
articles.body: The United States on Tuesday accused Chinese Artificial Intelligence firms, including DeepSeek and Alibaba, of stealing trade secrets of their American counterparts to cut development costs and swiftly release coveted technologies to the market.As per a joint advisory by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, National Security Agency, and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, major Chinese technology firms are extracting “restricted proprietary functionalities and capabilities of US frontier AI models", using "distillation" techniques, where smaller models are trained on more advanced architectures.The disclosures come as President Donald Trump prepares to discuss AI with Chinese leader Xi Jinping during his Washington visit, later this month.US Authorities and tech executives acknowledged that distillation can serve as a legitimate research method, but argued that the scale and targeted nature of Chinese efforts amounted to theft.The advisory stated that the scope and sophistication of these campaigns showed distillation was not merely supplementary but "the critical core" of these firms' AI development.Additionally, the agencies claimed that Chinese AI companies rely on a network of intermediaries, described as a "grey market of proxies known as 'transfer stations'", to bypass geographic limitations and safety measures put in place by US firms, with Alibaba Group and DeepSeek among the companies named as having run "high-volume knowledge distillation campaigns".US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent cautioned that penalties could follow, writing on X that sanctions and Entity List designations would be considered against Chinese firms found to have crossed "into IP theft" through covert, large-scale distillation.Separately, Anthropic reported that three Chinese AI laboratories had run an "industrial-scale campaign" to extract capabilities from its Claude model, generating over 16 million exchanges through roughly 24,000 fraudulent accounts.Adding to these concerns, a Google Threat Intelligence report published the same day found hackers increasingly targeting AI assets, warning that proprietary models and source code have become prime targets for espionage, extortion and resource theft.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In the early 1970s, schoolchildren released rabbits on an abandoned Japanese island; 50 years later, DNA suggested other people had repeatedly left unwanted pets there
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover the complex history of Okunoshima, Japan's Rabbit Island, where DNA testing unveils evidence of multiple introductions of domestic rabbits amidst a background of war and tourism.
articles.body: A small island in Japan’s Seto Inland Sea is now known as “Rabbit Island”, but its past is far darker. From 1929 until the end of the Second World War, the island was used by the Japanese Imperial Army for the secret production of poison gas. Today, hundreds of free-ranging European rabbits roam the island, drawing visitors who come to feed and photograph them.Eight rabbits and a mysteryThe most widely accepted account places the beginning of Okunoshima’s present rabbit population in 1971, when eight rabbits kept at a school were released on the island. Japan’s Environment Ministry says the release of eight rabbits that could no longer be kept at the school is considered the starting point of the island’s rabbit population. The animals were European domestic rabbits, rather than a species native to Japan. Nevertheless, another theory has followed the rabbits for decades. Because of the island’s history as a secret chemical weapons production site, a story has circulated that today’s rabbits are descendants of animals used in wartime experiments. This theory has never been proven. Rabbits were indeed used as test animals at the poison-gas facility, but accounts of their fate after the war differ. Some reports claimed that the test rabbits were released when the factory closed, while other accounts said they were killed or euthanised.Genetic research has made the rabbits’ origins even more intriguing. Rather than finding a clear genetic signature pointing to a single group of founders, researchers found evidence consistent with the population forming through multiple introductions over time. The scientists also noted considerable variation in the rabbits’ coat colours and types. According to the Journal of Ecotourism, the genetic evidence and the diversity of rabbits found on Okunoshima are consistent with the possibility that domestic rabbits were introduced to the island on multiple occasions. The findings do not establish the precise origin of every rabbit, but they suggest that the population may have been shaped by more than a single release.When tourism changed the islandAccording to Fukushima University, Okunoshima’s development as a tourist destination added another dimension to its relationship with the rabbits. The island is part of Setonaikai National Park, established in 1934, and developed as a leisure destination in the following decades. As its reputation as Rabbit Island grew, visitors began arriving specifically to see and feed the animals. Today, the rabbits rely at least partly on food supplied by people, and their population appears to be associated with tourism. Visitor numbers fell during the COVID-19 period, and rabbit numbers declined at the same time, which suggests the animals may have relied in part on food provided by tourists.The growing rabbit population has also created ecological pressures. Okunoshima has limited natural vegetation, while food provided for the rabbits can attract other animals. Researchers found that wild boars eat food intended for the rabbits and sometimes attack them. They also found that food provided to the rabbits could be encouraging this behaviour among wild boars, although they could not establish a direct causal link.A paradise with a complicated pastToday, visitors to Okunoshima encounter free-ranging rabbits alongside the remains of the island’s wartime poison-gas facilities. For years, the accepted account of the rabbits’ arrival was straightforward: eight domestic rabbits that had been kept at a school were released on the island in 1971 and multiplied over the following decades. But recent genetic evidence has complicated that story, suggesting that the present population may have been shaped by multiple introductions rather than a single release.The island’s history reflects several stages of human influence. Wartime poison-gas production altered Okunoshima’s landscape, while the introduction of domestic rabbits brought a non-native animal into its environment. Tourism later created another connection between people and the rabbits, with visitors supplying food that may have influenced the population. Visitor numbers fell during the COVID-19 period, and rabbit numbers declined at the same time, which suggests the animals may have relied in part on food provided by tourists. Okunoshima’s rabbits are therefore closely tied to both the island’s wartime past and the tourism that grew around them.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Civilisational twins’: Rajnath Singh meets Sri Lankan president, steps up India’s defence ties with Colombo
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Wednesday met Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in Colombo and discussed the multi-faceted pa.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Wednesday met Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in Colombo and discussed the multi-faceted partnership between the two countries, including cooperation to ensure the safety, security, peace and prosperity of the region.Singh arrived in Sri Lanka on Tuesday for a three-day visit. His visit is the first by an Indian defence minister to the island nation in 38 years.Singh conveyed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's greetings to Dissanayake and congratulated him on the completion of two years of his government. He also underlined the deep friendship between the people of India and Sri Lanka, based on their historical and civilisational links.“The two sides reaffirmed that as civilisational twins, close neighbours and maritime partners, India and Sri Lanka would continue to work together for their development and welfare of the people while working jointly to ensure the safety, security, peace and prosperity of the region,” the ministry of defence said.Singh described the meeting as “warm and extremely productive” in a post on X.Sri Lanka reiterates commitment to India's securityDissanayake recalled his interactions with Prime Minister Modi and reiterated that Sri Lanka would never allow its territory to be used for activities inimical to India's security interests, the ministry of defence said.The Sri Lankan president also expressed gratitude for India's relief assistance under Operation Sagar Bandhu during Cyclone Ditwah and the comprehensive rehabilitation package extended by New Delhi for reconstruction and rehabilitation.Singh said India considered assistance to Sri Lanka a responsibility rather than a favour.“As a closest friend and neighbour of Sri Lanka, India considered it not a favour, but a responsibility to assist as the first responder and would continue to do so in the future as well,” he said.Both leaders also virtually inaugurated three Bailey Bridges constructed by Indian defence forces.Defence cooperation gets fresh pushIndia and Sri Lanka exchanged memorandums of understanding on the upgradation of L70 guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force and cooperation between the National Cadet Corps (NCC) and National Defence Colleges (NDC) of both countries.The MoU on the upgradation of six L70 guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force falls under an Indian government grant. The Ministry of Defence said the upgraded air defence guns would strengthen the air defence architecture of critical assets in Sri Lanka.The guns had earlier been provided to the Sri Lanka Air Force by India.The academic cooperation agreement between the NDCs of India and Sri Lanka will facilitate knowledge sharing between the two institutions, the ministry said.The NCC cooperation agreement will formalise the NCC youth exchange programme between India and Sri Lanka. The programme provides an opportunity for NCC cadets from multiple countries to travel to New Delhi each year and participate in NCC events.Singh is leading a high-level delegation comprising senior officials from the ministries of defence and external affairs.Sri Lankan opposition backs stronger India tiesSingh's visit also included an interaction with the Indian diaspora in Colombo, where he said India would stand firmly with Sri Lanka during times of crisis.“The relationship between India and Sri Lanka is based on shared history, culture, and faith. We stand with Sri Lanka through thick and thin and are committed to the peace, prosperity, and development of both countries,” Singh said, according to news agency ANI.Sri Lanka's leader of opposition Sajith Premadasa also praised India's support for the island nation after meeting Singh, describing India as a “very close partner” and the bilateral relationship as “very special”.“My meeting with Rajnath Singh was very constructive, very progressive. We have a very strong relationship with India. It is a special relationship. We are very close partners,” Premadasa said.He highlighted India's role as a first responder during Sri Lanka's economic crisis, the Covid-19 pandemic and Cyclone Ditwah.“India has always been the first responder. And Prime Minister Modi has always walked the talk. India has been the first responder in supporting Sri Lanka during Ditwah, during times of bankruptcy, and during the Corona health hazard,” Premadasa said.Premadasa said Colombo wanted to further deepen ties with India while respecting the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of both countries.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Nepal’s flood bill could hit $5 billion. Where will the money come from?
articles.summary: South Asia News: It's been more than 10 days since a glacial collapse sent freezing water, rocks and debris roaring down Nepal's Bhotekoshi and Trishuli valleys.The de.
articles.body: It's been more than 10 days since a glacial collapse sent freezing water, rocks and debris roaring down Nepal's Bhotekoshi and Trishuli valleys.The death toll has risen to 1,357, while 5,326 people remain missing, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority. Rescue teams have so far saved 13,583 people.The disaster has also inflicted an enormous economic cost. Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority estimates that the floods caused NPR 387.54 billion ($2.56 billion) in damage to property, housing and infrastructure. The government says its immediate four-month recovery effort will require another NPR 7.95 billion, or about $53 million, for roads, temporary shelters, drinking water and electricity.But that is only the beginning.Nepal's finance minister Swarnim Wagle told Reuters that the eventual reconstruction bill could reach $4 billion to $5 billion, roughly a tenth of Nepal's annual economic output. The figure remains preliminary and could change as authorities complete detailed assessments.For a country with an economy of about $46 billion, the scale of the challenge is daunting.Nepal is not entering the crisis with unlimited fiscal room. It is still dealing with the legacy of the 2015 earthquake, while public debt has risen sharply over the past decade.The question now is simple but difficult: Where will the money to rebuild come from?A tight fiscal positionNepal's government will have to shoulder part of the cost itself.It can reprioritise spending, use existing disaster-response resources and increase borrowing. But each option comes with a price.The IMF estimates Nepal's public debt at 49.6% of GDP in FY2025-26, up from 48.1% a year earlier. It also expects the country to continue running a fiscal deficit as the government seeks to increase revenue and improve public-investment execution.A large reconstruction programme would therefore compete with spending on schools, hospitals, jobs and other infrastructure.Borrowing could help bridge part of the gap, but greater reliance on debt would increase future debt-servicing costs and leave less room for development spending.Nepal therefore needs not just money, but financing that can be mobilised quickly and channelled into reconstruction projects.An economy already under strainThe disaster has hit sectors that Nepal has been relying on to strengthen its economy.Remittances remain the country's biggest external financial cushion. The IMF expects workers' remittances to reach $15.2 billion in FY2025-26, equivalent to 33.1 per cent of GDP.But remittances are household income, not government revenue. They support consumption and provide foreign exchange, but Kathmandu cannot simply redirect that money towards rebuilding public infrastructure.That makes sectors such as hydropower and tourism especially important to the recovery.Hydropower has been one of Nepal's biggest growth opportunities, with the country seeking to harness its Himalayan rivers to generate electricity and expand exports to India. But at least 11 hydropower projects in the affected corridor have been damaged, knocking generating capacity offline.Tourism faces a different risk. Nepal's trekking, mountaineering and pilgrimage industries depend heavily on access to mountain regions. Damaged roads and bridges could therefore disrupt visitor flows and hurt another important source of foreign exchange.Nepal now has to rebuild while some of the very sectors expected to drive future growth have themselves taken a hit.Domestic financing: The first layerThe first layer of the reconstruction effort will come from Nepal's own resources.The government can reprioritise its budget, divert spending towards damaged infrastructure and draw on disaster-response funds. It can also increase domestic or external borrowing.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();But these resources will not be enough on their own.The government will have to decide what gets rebuilt first. Roads and bridges reconnecting isolated communities, electricity infrastructure and housing for displaced families are likely to take priority over projects that can wait.Nepal's own resources will therefore form the foundation of the financing package, rather than cover the entire reconstruction bill.Insurance and private capitalCommercial assets provide another, albeit more limited, source of funding.Hydropower projects and other insured businesses can receive payouts for physical damage and, in some cases, business interruption.Nepal's Insurance Authority had received 583 flood-related claims worth NPR 25.87 billion ($171 million) as of August 31. The figure represents reported claims and insured exposure rather than final payouts, with assessments still under way.Hydropower projects are expected to account for a significant share of those claims, given the concentration of damage along the affected river corridors.Insurance payouts could help companies repair or replace damaged assets, but they cannot finance public infrastructure such as roads, bridges and settlements.Private investment could provide another source of capital, particularly for hydropower. Companies can raise equity, borrow against future electricity revenues and use insurance proceeds to restore damaged facilities.But private capital has a natural limit.An investor can finance a power plant because it can sell electricity and generate a return. There is far less incentive to finance a remote road or bridge that provides a public benefit but generates no direct revenue.Public infrastructure will therefore continue to depend heavily on government and donor financing.Development banks: The biggest external poolThe largest external financing pool is likely to come from international development institutions.The UN and humanitarian partners have already appealed for $49.6 million to help more than 84,000 people with food, shelter, healthcare, clean water and cash assistance over four months. The Asian Development Bank has separately approved a $5 million emergency grant.But these are emergency funds, not long-term reconstruction financing.For the rebuilding phase, Kathmandu can turn to institutions such as the World Bank and ADB for concessional loans, grants and project financing.Nepal already has a disaster-financing mechanism with the World Bank. In 2024, the bank approved $150 million in contingent financing under a Catastrophe Deferred Drawdown Option, allowing the government to access funds after a qualifying natural disaster.Such instruments can provide immediate liquidity. But a reconstruction programme running into several billion dollars would require fresh commitments from multilateral lenders, bilateral donors and other development partners.Bilateral aidNepal is also receiving assistance directly from other countries, although most of it so far has focused on emergency relief and rescue rather than long-term reconstruction.The UK has offered £5 million ($6.8 million) in aid, while South Korea has pledged $1 million in humanitarian assistance. The US initially committed $500,000 and later increased its contribution to $3.6 million for food and emergency supplies.India has provided relief supplies, rescue personnel and technical assistance, including more than 68 tonnes of relief material.Nepal's foreign ministry says it has received support from a wider group of countries, including Japan, Australia, Germany, Qatar, the UAE, China and Canada. It has also said Nepal has received monetary pledges from international partners, although the government has not published a consolidated country-by-country tally as of now.These contributions are significant for the immediate response. But the next phase will require something much larger: bilateral grants, concessional financing and project-specific support for reconstruction.For Kathmandu, grants would be particularly valuable because they would not add to its debt burden. But bilateral aid alone cannot close the financing gap.Climate finance: Another potential sourceAnother potential source of funding is the international "loss and damage" fund, created after years of demands from vulnerable developing countries that they should receive financial support for climate-related destruction they did little to cause.The fund was agreed at the UN climate summit in Egypt in 2022 and formally operationalised at COP28 in Dubai in 2023. At COP28, countries agreed that the World Bank would host the fund temporarily and administer it as a financial intermediary.Governments contribute to the fund, but those contributions are voluntary rather than a mandatory bill imposed on particular countries. More than $720 million had been pledged by COP29 in 2024.Nepal is now seeking access to that money. Its foreign minister has called for $20 million from the loss-and-damage mechanism following the floods, arguing that Nepal contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse-gas emissions while facing severe climate risks.However, $20 million would cover only a tiny fraction of a potential $4 billion-$5 billion reconstruction bill.The loss-and-damage fund can therefore provide an additional source of financing, but it is unlikely to come close to funding Nepal's entire recovery.The government is also turning to Parliament to assess in more specific terms how the disaster could affect Nepal’s economy and how it can tap climate finance. A seven-member Finance Committee sub-panel, formed on Wednesday (September 9), has been asked to study the economic impact of the August 26 floods and issues related to climate finance, with its report due by September 18.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The 2015 earthquake offers a blueprintNepal has a precedent for financing reconstruction on a multibillion-dollar scale.The 2015 earthquake caused around $7 billion in physical damage and generated reconstruction needs estimated at roughly $6.7 billion.At an international conference that year, donors and development partners pledged about $4.1 billion for Nepal's reconstruction. The World Bank alone committed up to $500 million.That experience offers the clearest indication of what a financing package for the current disaster could look like.Nepal would put some of its own resources into reconstruction, while development partners provide grants and concessional loans and private investors finance commercially viable projects.But there is one major difference: Nepal now has a much larger debt burden than it did before the 2015 earthquake.That makes the terms of external financing particularly important. Grants and highly concessional loans would place significantly less pressure on government finances than commercial borrowing.The cost that cannot be countedNepal is therefore facing a financing stack rather than a single source of money.The scale of the destruction means these sources will have to be combined and coordinated. To avoid substantially increasing its debt burden, Kathmandu will need a much larger international financing package, including grants and other assistance that does not have to be repaid, alongside concessional loans and other forms of financing.Even then, the $4 billion-$5 billion reconstruction estimate will not capture every cost.The economic loss from thousands of deaths and missing people, for instance, extends far beyond the value of damaged property and infrastructure. Families can lose their main source of income when a breadwinner dies, while survivors may face injuries, displacement, interrupted work and psychological trauma.Children may lose schooling. Businesses may lose workers and customers.These losses are much harder to quantify than a damaged road or power plant, but they can prolong the economic impact of the disaster for years.The resilience questionThere is one more complication: the final bill could rise if Nepal decides to rebuild differently.Replacing a bridge with another bridge in the same vulnerable location may restore a transport link quickly, but it does little to reduce the risk of another disaster.The World Bank estimates that Nepal needs $47.4 billion in adaptation investment between 2021 and 2050. That figure covers the country's much broader climate-adaptation requirements and should not be confused with the current flood reconstruction bill.For Kathmandu, rebuilding presents a fundamental choice: replace damaged infrastructure as quickly and cheaply as possible, or spend more to make it more resilient.The second option may require greater upfront investment, but it could reduce the cost of future disasters.That choice is also likely to shape Nepal's international financing appeal. Donors and development banks have increasingly linked reconstruction funding to resilience, disaster-risk reduction and climate adaptation.For now, Nepal's immediate challenge is to finance a potential $5 billion reconstruction bill.Its bigger challenge is to ensure that the money does not simply rebuild what the floods destroyed, but helps build infrastructure capable of withstanding what comes next.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'They have no position': China's note lands mid-speech; Philippines defence chief fires back on stage
articles.summary: Rest of World News: NEW DELHI: Philippines defence secretary Gilberto C Teodoro publicly rebuked China at a defence forum in Seoul after a note outlining Beijing's positi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Philippines defence secretary Gilberto C Teodoro publicly rebuked China at a defence forum in Seoul after a note outlining Beijing's position on the South China Sea arbitration was handed to him while he was speaking.Teodoro was addressing maritime challenges and the South China Sea at the Seoul Defence Dialogue when a man approached him from behind and placed a sheet of paper on the table. Teodoro paused, picked up the note and asked whether it had come from China before reading parts of it aloud. "I have a note here. I think this is from China. And may I read it?" he said.As Teodoro read the note, he interrupted its argument with a blunt response: "They have no position." The note stated that China's position on the South China Sea arbitration was "clear, consistent and firm" and argued that the arbitration violated fundamental principles of international law.Teodoro then challenged the legal argument contained in the note, referring to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), under which the Philippines had brought the arbitration case against China. "So what you signed unclause. You mean violates international law. That's what you mean," he said.The note further described the arbitration ruling as illegal, null and void and said it had no binding force. The 2016 arbitration tribunal rejected China's expansive historic-rights claims in the South China Sea and found no legal basis for Beijing's claims to resources within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone. China has rejected the ruling and maintained that the tribunal had no jurisdiction.The Philippine defence chief then turned the incident into a broader criticism of Beijing's conduct, questioning the decision to deliver the message while he was addressing an international audience."How can you deal with a country in an international forum beyond the question asked to me disrespecting the organizers of this forum, how do you expect to deal with it civilly?" Teodoro said.He argued that the episode went beyond the legal dispute and amounted to a lack of respect for the forum's organisers and South Korea, which was hosting the event."If this is a Chinese position sent to me, it not only disrespects international law throwing uncloths to the floor and trampling upon it, but it also disrespects the basic decency accorded that should be accorded to our most gracious hosts, the Republic of Korea and the rest of the audience here," he said.Teodoro then accused China of using pressure against the Philippines, saying, "Perhaps basic decency and behavior is what China needs to do now."He said he would retain the note as a reminder of what he described as Beijing's weakness in making its case."I will keep this paper as a memento of how desperate China is and how ineffective its position is in the face of a free audience," Teodoro said.He also directed a sarcastic remark at the person who had handed over the note, saying, "You just done your country a great service. Thank you. And I hope you don't suffer in a gulag for it."What initially appeared to be a deliberate interruption was later reported to have resulted from a mix-up.According to forum organisers, the note had been sent by a Chinese military attache with the Chinese Embassy in Seoul, Yonhap News Agency reported. The attache reportedly handed it to a forum staff member with instructions that it be passed to Teodoro.The staff member apparently mistook it for a message from Teodoro's own delegation and handed it to him while he was speaking.Teodoro targets China's South China Sea claimsTeodoro used the episode to reiterate Manila's concerns over China's activities in the South China Sea, particularly in areas that the Philippines considers part of its exclusive economic zone."I think it is well known to the public, to everyone here, about the Philippine situation where we face challenges daily from the People's Republic of China, which tries to occupy and illegally assert its presence over our territory and especially our exclusive economic zone," he said.He said the Philippines had responded by strengthening its defence arrangements and alliances."We live in a very interconnected world, and there is no right for any state of that matter to appropriate an international common for its exclusive use or right, contrary to what the international norms clearly state," Teodoro said.China later sought to distance itself from the circumstances surrounding the note while reiterating its established position on the arbitration case."We advise some people in the Philippines to stop trying to stir up trouble, stop undermining bilateral ties and stability in the South China Sea," the Chinese Foreign Ministry said, without naming Teodoro.The incident, which began with a single sheet of paper being placed on Teodoro's table, quickly became a public confrontation over China's position on the South China Sea and the Philippines' refusal to accept Beijing's claims.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Cheaper homes, faster clearances: Real estate experts lay out reforms for future growth
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: India’s real estate sector needs faster approvals, digitised land records and a dedicated affordable housing policy to tackle rising home p.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s real estate sector needs faster approvals, digitised land records and a dedicated affordable housing policy to tackle rising home prices and improve ease of doing business, industry experts said at an ASSOCHAM conference on Tuesday.Speaking at the National Conference on Real Estate for Viksit Bharat: Enabling Growth, Investment & Ease of Doing Business, industry representatives said regulatory and policy reforms were needed to make housing more affordable and support the sector’s future growth.The experts identified rising land prices, lengthy approval processes and outdated land records as key hurdles facing the sector. They called for greater use of technology and a single-window system to simplify project approvals.Affordable housing policy neededAshwinder R Singh, Chairman of the CII Real Estate Committee, Northern Region, said rising land prices were making affordable housing increasingly difficult.“Affordable housing is a complex issue. Land prices have gone up. There are certain policy interventions required,” Singh said.He said the government and private sector were already working on the issue, but a more focused policy was needed.“There’s a lot of work happening both in the private sector and the public sector, and the government is involved. But this is a big headwind that needs to be resolved quickly, and we need to come out with an affordable housing policy that kind of addresses this,” he added.Singh said the urgency had increased as home prices continued to move beyond the reach of many ordinary buyers.“Because the current home prices are going out of bounds for the common man, which is a fact. We have to address this. If we don't talk about it, there will never be a solution around it,” he said.Faster approvals, digitised land recordsPradeep Aggarwal, Chairman of the National Council on Real Estate, Housing, Urban Development, said improving ease of doing business should be another priority.“There are challenges around approvals, especially the long-standing demand for single-window clearance. Land records need to be digitised, approvals need to become faster, and technology adoption needs to improve,” Aggarwal said.A single-window approval system could reduce delays for developers by bringing multiple clearances under one process. Digitised land records could also make transactions more transparent and reduce disputes.Aggarwal said reforms should also focus on how buildings are designed and operated. The industry, he said, was moving beyond simply adding more structures towards smarter and more sustainable development.“The focus is not just on building structures, but on making buildings smarter and more sustainable,” he said.Developers are increasingly adopting green building practices and other technology-led solutions, Aggarwal added, with their impact expected to become more visible in the coming years.The industry’s demands therefore centre on three broad areas: making land and housing more affordable, cutting approval delays and using technology to make real estate development more transparent and efficient.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: SIR row: No notice issued to Prof CNR Rao over name discrepancy, says Bengaluru official
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: No notice was issued to Bharat Ratna awardee and renowned scientist Prof C N R Rao over a discrepancy in his name in the electoral roll dur.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: No notice was issued to Bharat Ratna awardee and renowned scientist Prof C N R Rao over a discrepancy in his name in the electoral roll during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) chief commissioner M Maheshwar Rao said on Wednesday, as cited by news agency PTI.Clarifying the matter, the GBA said in a statement that the booth level officer (BLO) did not issue any notice to Rao. Instead, the officer recommended that his name be retained in the final electoral roll."No notice has been issued to the Hon’ble Bharat Ratna (awardee) Prof C N (R) Rao in connection with the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls in the Malleshwaram assembly constituency," the GBA said, quoting Maheshwar Rao, who also serves as the district election officer of Bengaluru Urban.As part of the SIR exercise, enumeration forms were personally delivered to Rao and his family members at their residence by the State SVEEP Nodal Officer along with the Commissioner of the Bengaluru West City Corporation. The required details were subsequently filled in.According to the GBA, Rao was listed as a voter in Part No-129, Serial No-431 of the 76-Malleshwaram assembly constituency in the 2002 electoral roll. His name at the time was recorded as ‘Rama’.Explaining the discrepancy, the authority said the BLO decided against issuing a notice and instead recommended retaining Rao's name in the final roll."A discrepancy was noticed in the name of the Hon’ble person in the electoral roll. In view of this, the Booth Level Officer (BLO), without issuing any notice, has recommended inclusion of his name in the final electoral roll, considering him to be a respected person. Accordingly, necessary action has been initiated to include his name in the final electoral roll," the GBA said.He is currently enrolled as a voter in Part No-59, Serial No-187 of the 157-Malleshwaram assembly constituency under the name 'Prof CN Rao M'. The GBA said his name has consequently been included in the draft electoral roll.The clarification came after reports suggested that Rao had received a notice in connection with the electoral roll revision.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Priscilla Chan helped protect a centuries-old Hawaiian fishpond with a $4 million gift; the land will remain a community conservation site
articles.summary: US News: A 600-year-old Hawaiian fishpond that faced the possibility of development is now permanently protected as a community conservation site after a $4 mi.
articles.body: A 600-year-old Hawaiian fishpond that faced the possibility of development is now permanently protected as a community conservation site after a $4 million charitable gift from Priscilla Chan and Mark Zuckerberg helped fund its acquisition. Alakoko Fishpond, also known as Alekoko or Menehune Fishpond, covers 102 acres in Niumalu near Līhuʻe on Kauaʻi. It features a 2,700-foot-long kuapā, or fishpond wall, and is the largest remaining fishpond on Kauaʻi. The Trust for Public Land purchased the property on November 17, 2021, and then conveyed it to the community-based nonprofit Mālama Hulē‘ia for community and cultural stewardship. The deed ensures the land will remain dedicated to conservation, education and community purposes in perpetuity.The $4 million gift that helped save a 600-year-old Hawaiian fishpondThe conservation effort accelerated after Alakoko and its surrounding 102 acres were placed on the market in January 2021, raising concerns that the culturally important landscape could be developed. The Trust for Public Land and Mālama Hulē‘ia had already been working to protect the site and had been seeking public funding for its acquisition. More than 5,500 people signed an online statement supporting permanent protection, while hundreds of community members and organisations submitted written testimony. The Kauaʻi County Open Space Commission unanimously supported the project in February 2021, but securing county funding would have required additional steps. With the property on the open market, TPL also sought private philanthropic support. Chan and Zuckerberg then committed a $4 million charitable gift through the Chan Zuckerberg Kauaʻi Community Fund of the Hawaiʻi Community Foundation. The donation provided full funding for the conservation purchase, transaction expenses and support for the missions of TPL and Mālama Hulē‘ia, allowing the purchase to move ahead quickly.An ancient fishpond with a deep cultural historyAlakoko is believed to date back around six centuries and is a traditional Hawaiian loko kuapā, or walled fishpond. Its 2,700-foot kuapā forms the defining structure of the pond. The site is also known as Menehune Fishpond because Hawaiian legends say the Menehune, described in traditional stories as skilled builders and among Hawaiʻi's earliest inhabitants, constructed it. The legend should be understood as part of the site's cultural tradition rather than as a literal archaeological account of its construction. The fishpond itself is a documented historic and cultural resource. For generations, Alakoko served as a source of fish and limu, or seaweed, and represented a traditional system of managing natural resources and producing food. TPL describes Native Hawaiian fishpond systems as important examples of Hawaiian ingenuity in food sovereignty and natural-resource management.Years of neglect had damaged the ecosystemThe fishpond had deteriorated over decades as invasive mangroves spread through the area. TPL says the mangroves had engulfed parts of the fishpond and hindered native natural systems and species. Alakoko is adjacent to the Hulēʻia National Wildlife Refuge and forms part of a wider wetland and estuary environment supporting native fish, limu, coastal vegetation and endangered Hawaiian water birds. The site's historical importance was formally recognised when Alakoko was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1973. In 2009, the Historic Hawaiʻi Foundation designated it one of Hawaiʻi's most endangered historic places because of its vulnerability to environmental degradation and development. Before the property was permanently protected, Mālama Hulē‘ia had already spent four years working with the community to restore the fishpond and its surrounding native wetland and estuary.The land is returning to community stewardshipThe conservation purchase was completed by the Trust for Public Land on November 17, 2021. TPL then transferred the property to Mālama Hulē‘ia, a community-based nonprofit that works to restore the Hulēʻia ecosystem and promote environmental stewardship based on Hawaiian values. Chan and Zuckerberg did not receive ownership of the land. Instead, their charitable donation made it possible for TPL to secure the property and transfer it into long-term community stewardship. The deed requires Alakoko to be used for conservation, education and community purposes in perpetuity. Mālama Hulē‘ia plans to continue restoring the fishpond, surrounding wetlands and wildlife habitat while developing the site as a place for community gatherings and cultural activities.A working fishpond and outdoor classroom for future generationsThe long-term vision goes beyond preserving Alakoko as a historic landmark. Mālama Hulē‘ia plans to restore it as a working fishpond where fish and seafood can once again be grown and harvested, helping provide a sustainable food source for Kauaʻi. The organisation also intends to use the site as an outdoor classroom where students can learn about native ecosystems, traditional Hawaiian aquaculture, history and culture. TPL says the project is intended to create both sustainable food and learning opportunities while protecting 102 acres of culturally and environmentally significant land. The restoration is expected to be a multi-generational effort, with the community continuing to care for the fishpond and surrounding ecosystem.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Warning after battery causes bin lorry fire in Lincoln
articles.summary: Lincoln County Council is warning of the dangers of putting batteries in waste collections.
articles.body:
Firefighters tackled a blaze in a bin lorry caused by an "improperly disposed battery", Lincolnshire Fire and Rescue Service has said.

Two fire engines attended the incident on Elvington Road in Lincoln at about 10:25 BST on Tuesday.

Photographs and video footage show a pile of waste burning by the roadside.

Lincolnshire County Council is warning of the dangers of putting batteries in waste collections and said they should be disposed of at recycling centres.

Rachel Stamp, waste partnership and projects manager at the council, said: "Batteries are hazardous waste, they can leak chemicals, cause fires and even explode when crushed or compacted with other rubbish.

"We see several fires in waste collection lorries and household waste recycling centres across the county. All these put our staff and firefighters who attended in danger and often closed sites and cancelled routes.

"Most people are doing the right thing, which is to bring your batteries and electrical waste to our household waste recycling centres and put it in the correct areas, but unfortunately, it only takes one battery in a compactor to start a fire."

It is one of several instances of fires in bin lorries caused by batteries in the county over the last few years.

articles.title: ‘Designed for the China fight’: Silicon Valley-backed startup unveils low-cost, mass-produced cruise missile as US stocks strain
articles.summary: International News: US defence startup Covenant plans to begin mass production of its low-cost Anthem cruise missile in Germany in early 2027, targeting European demand f.
articles.body: US defence startup Covenant plans to begin mass production of its low-cost Anthem cruise missile in Germany in early 2027, targeting European demand for long-range weapons as the United States and its allies seek to replenish advanced munitions stocks depleted by recent conflicts.Covenant says Anthem has been designed for rapid, high-volume production at a lower cost than comparable weapons made by major defence contractors. Its Saxony facility is expected to initially produce 1,000 missiles a year from 2027, eventually reaching a capacity of 5,000 annually, company executives told news agency Reuters.The announcement comes amid growing concern over US stockpiles of advanced weapons following sustained military operations, including the war with Iran.Multiple reports have highlighted concerns among US military commanders over critically low stocks of certain munitions, particularly air-defence interceptors.On September 6, US government investigators had subjected around 50 members of the military's Joint Staff to polygraph tests during an investigation into leaks to journalists, including reports concerning the war with Iran and the depletion of critical US munitions stocks.Covenant is pitching Anthem as a response to the production and cost constraints surrounding high-end missiles.“Comparable weapons from the biggest defense contractors are "being built in small quantities at really high ​prices. And so we set out to change that,"” Michael Kaufman, Covenant's co-founder and chief executive officer, told Reuters.Anthem is a ground-launched cruise missile carrying a payload of more than 200 kg. It uses a solid rocket motor for launch and a heavy-fuel jet engine for cruise flight, and has flown the missile more than 200 times in tests over the past year.The company is targeting a mid-six-figure price per missile once full-rate production begins. It has already booked roughly $150 million in orders and expects to begin generating revenue in 2027.Covenant said it has sought to build a supply chain capable of supporting mass production, including three solid-rocket-motor providers and a fourth in development. It has also signed long-term agreements covering more than 4,000 jet engines over the next two years.The company's Dallas plant, spanning 105,000 square feet, is expected to reach production of 5,000 missiles a year. Its German facility is planned for the same eventual capacity, while a smaller plant in northern Israel will produce 2,000 annually.Covenant president Abby Denburg said the missile had been developed with a potential Indo-Pacific conflict in mind.“We were designed for the China fight,” she told the news agency.Covenant also said it is developing a naval version of Anthem and expects Germany and other European countries to require tens of thousands of long-range weapons.

articles.title: ‘Quit politics completely’: Mayawati’s message to Ashok Siddharth as Akash Anand awaits big BSP role ahead of 2027 UP polls
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: BSP national president Mayawati said on Tuesday that Ashok Siddharth, the father-in-law of her nephew Akash Anand, should take complete \"sany.
articles.body: LUCKNOW: BSP national president Mayawati said on Tuesday that Ashok Siddharth, the father-in-law of her nephew Akash Anand, should take complete "sanyas" from politics. Only then, she said, would it be appropriate for Akash Anand to work freely in the party again.Akash Anand was the BSP's national convener until September 3, when Mayawati announced at an all-India meeting of party office-bearers that he would work as an ordinary party worker. She said it would not be appropriate to give him any major responsibility, adding that he still needed to become more "mature."Mayawati said on Tuesday that the party leadership will consider giving Akash Anand's responsibilities back to him only after Ashok Siddharth gives up politics completely.Ashok Siddharth, a former Rajya Sabha MP of the party, was expelled by Mayawati on August 2 for alleged anti-party activities.What happened on September 3At the September 3 meeting, Mayawati told BSP office-bearers: "I have allowed Akash Anand to work in the party, which is before all of you, but Akash Anand still needs to become more mature. Till then, it would not be appropriate to give him a major responsibility in the party."She said Akash Anand, as national coordinator, would continue to work in the party. Mayawati invoked BSP founder Kanshi Ram's approach of allowing family members to assist with party work but opposing giving them election tickets or positions after the party came to power. "I am also completely committed to that resolve," she said.At the same meeting, Mayawati announced that the BSP has decided to contest all elections across the country on its own, without alliances. She also described the Congress as "strongly anti-Dalit and anti-Ambedkar" and criticised the RSS, citing recent remarks by its chief Mohan Bhagwat during his US visit.Both Akash Anand and Ishan Anand, Mayawati's younger nephew, attended the September 3 meeting.The reshuffle around himIn the same period, Mayawati has brought back several previously expelled leaders into the party fold.Former national coordinator Randhir Singh Beniwal, expelled in August for alleged anti-party activities and indiscipline, has rejoined the BSP and been assigned as central coordinator responsible for organising the party in selected states. Senior leader Ashok Siddharth was removed at the same time as Beniwal but remains outside the party.Dharamveer Ashok, a former minister in the Mayawati-led UP government in 2007 and a former member of the legislative council, was expelled in April on similar charges and was readmitted in August.Meerut-based leaders Mohit Anand and Nitin Singh have also been named central coordinators. Singh was expelled last year and reinstated a few months later.Party sources said Mayawati is expanding the BSP's organisation at the national and state levels, with several returning leaders appointed as central coordinators to build cadres, oversee outreach, and strengthen the party's footprint in their allotted states.Ishan Anand may get his first party roleMayawati has also dropped hints that she may appoint Ishan Anand, her younger nephew, as in charge of Sector-1 and Sector-2 in the party organisation, according to sources aware of a late-night meeting of national-level office-bearers held at her residence. No official announcement has been made.Sector-1 and Sector-2 cover all state units except Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, which remain under Mayawati's direct supervision. If confirmed, the role would be Ishan Anand's first formal responsibility in the BSP.Ishan Anand, 27, is a graduate in legal studies from the University of Westminster in the UK. He made his first public appearance on the party stage on January 15, 2025, during Mayawati's birthday event, and attended a state-level meeting of the BSP's UP unit the next day — seen at the time as a signal of his growing involvement ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.The election contextThe developments come ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly election and the subsequent Uttar Pradesh assembly election. On August 25, Mayawati announced that the BSP would contest the Punjab polls "alone without any alliance or compromise with anyone," saying electoral tie-ups risked weakening the party's vote share and demoralising its cadre.The decision is significant for the BSP in Punjab, where founder Kanshi Ram began his political journey and where Scheduled Castes account for 31.94% of the population — the highest proportion of any state, according to the 2011 Census. articles.title: ‘Unfounded accusations’: China rejects US claims of 'malicious' AI distillation by its firms
articles.summary: US News: China on Wednesday rejected US allegations that its artificial intelligence companies are engaged in “aggressive, malicious” efforts to extract capabi.
articles.body: China on Wednesday rejected US allegations that its artificial intelligence companies are engaged in “aggressive, malicious” efforts to extract capabilities from advanced American AI models, calling on Washington to stop making what it described as unfounded accusations.The Ministry of Foreign Affairs urged the US to “refrain from making unfounded accusations or smears” against China. It added that both China and the US are major AI powers and should strengthen cooperation.According to the Associated Press, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said China’s AI development resulted from “high-level technological self-reliance and strength” and urged all sides to promote AI development that is open, inclusive and beneficial.Mao’s comments came a day after the FBI, National Security Agency (NSA) and Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) issued a joint cybersecurity advisory accusing Chinese AI developers of “distilling” capabilities from leading US models since at least late 2024.The advisory named Chinese companies including DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot AI and Z.AI and said their activities were “likely” carried out with Chinese government awareness. US agencies alleged that the companies had sought to extract capabilities from models including Anthropic’s Claude, OpenAI’s GPT, Google’s Gemini and xAI’s Grok.The latest exchange comes ahead of planned talks later this month between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, where AI governance is expected to be among the issues discussed.What US agencies said about Chinese AI firmsThe US agencies alleged that Chinese AI companies routed distillation requests through multiple channels to obtain unauthorised access to American AI models, potentially violating their terms of use.They also accused the companies of using shared premium subscriptions to reduce the cost of large-scale distillation efforts. The advisory described the activity as an industrial-scale effort to extract restricted capabilities from US frontier AI systems.The allegations add to earlier claims by American AI companies and officials that Chinese developers have used distillation to accelerate the development of their own models.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Tuesday said China would not overtake the US in AI, arguing that Chinese companies were distilling American models.“The Chinese distill our models, and they can never get ahead of us,” Bessent said at an event at Southern Methodist University’s Cox School of Business in Dallas, Texas.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange strikes as two killed at Moldova border
articles.summary: Meanwhile, four people, including a child, were killed in the southern Russian city of Novorossiysk.
articles.body:
Two people have been killed after Russian drones struck a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said.

The Starokozache crossing, around 500km (310 miles) south of Kyiv, was closed after the overnight attack. Images from the scene showed several cars left completely scorched, with wreckage and debris strewn across the border post.

Meanwhile, four people, including a child, were killed in the southern Russian city of Novorossiysk in a Ukrainian drone attack, the regional governor said.

Both Russia and Ukraine have stepped up long-range strikes in recent months, despite renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war.

Zelensky renewed calls for international support in the wake of the Starokozache crossing attack, saying "the aggression must be stopped here and now before it spreads any further".

The border link between Ukraine and Moldova was shut after the attack killed two people and injured three others, Odesa regional governor Oleg Kiper said.

A Moldovan driver was also injured, according to the country's foreign ministry.

Moldova has increasingly found itself caught up in the conflict, with Prime Minister Vasile Tofan confirming that 17 drones had struck Moldovan territory in August alone - more than during the whole of last year.

"Those who ignore or downplay these threats - and refuse to name the aggressor - are denying reality," he wrote on social media.

"Russia started this war. Russia alone bears responsibility."

Russia's defence ministry said its forces had shot down 596 Ukrainian drones overnight.

Novorossiysk – in the south of the country on the Black Sea coast - was hit hardest in what governor Veniamin Kondratiev described as a "massive overnight enemy drone attack".

As well as the four deaths, 29 people were injured, and damage was reported to residential buildings, a church and a preschool.

The strikes came a day after Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke to US President Donald Trump by phone about efforts to end the conflict.

The Trump administration has been pressing for direct talks between Russia and Ukraine, with Kyiv saying they could take place this month. The Kremlin, however, has said it is too early to discuss a date or venue.

The call followed talks between US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff and Putin in Moscow, before the pair travelled to Kyiv for meetings with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

articles.summary: A student’s emotional video from Noida International Airport in Greater Noida has triggered a debate about the passenger experience at the newly inaug.
articles.body: A student’s emotional video from Noida International Airport in Greater Noida has triggered a debate about the passenger experience at the newly inaugurated airport. In the video, the female student says she had a 6:15 AM flight to Jaipur. Despite reaching the airport around 5 AM and completing check-in and repeatedly requesting assistance, she missed the flight. The student claims she requested at the airport to let her travel without luggage because she had an exam at her college in Jaipur, her requests were not addressed.Now her sobbing video has since gone viral and shared widely across social media.What happenedAs per video, the student says she was travelling for an examination in an early-morning flight to Jaipur. She further says that she had an exam to write and was visibly distressed by the situation.The student is heard questioning the airport’s arrangements and expressing frustration at what she describes as a lack of assistance from airport management. At the end of the video, she swears she would not want to travel through Noida International Airport ever again.However, the exact circumstances surrounding the incident have not been independently established. As per a report published in Amar Ujala, the date of the video could not be confirmed and that there was no verified information available about the student’s name or any other detail. The report also said there had been no response from the airport management on the specific incident at the time of publication.What does Noida International Airport say about check-in?The incident also raises questions because the airport's official passenger guidance advises travellers to arrive at least two hours before a domestic flight. Its website says passengers checking in at the airport can complete check-in, drop baggage and collect their boarding pass at the airline's designated counter.The airport also offers self-service facilities and DigiYatra. Its official DigiYatra guidance specifically says that passengers travelling light can skip the check-in process and proceed directly towards security, while passengers with checked baggage can use the airline counter or self-baggage-drop facility where available.That makes the student's account particularly significant from a passenger-experience perspective.A newly opened airportNoida International Airport began commercial operations on June 15, 2026, with IndiGo operating the first commercial flight. The airport was designed as a major aviation gateway for Delhi-NCR and western Uttar Pradesh, with Phase 1 planned to handle up to 12 million passengers annually.The airport's official website highlights a range of passenger facilities, including Wi-Fi, lounges, food and beverage outlets, retail services, DigiYatra and accessibility assistance. It also says the airport has been designed around a modern, passenger-centric travel experience.The viral student's experience remains her account, rather than a verified finding against the airport. Yet the emotional reaction has struck a chord because airports ultimately succeed on something passengers can immediately feel: whether they are being heard when they need help.For Noida International Airport, which is still in the early months of commercial operations, that may be one of the most important lessons emerging from the viral video — a world-class terminal can only feel world-class when the passenger experience matches it.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Lincoln honeymoon couple en route to Maldives stranded at Stansted
articles.summary: Sam and Dan Stansfield are among tens of thousands affected by an air traffic control 'glitch'.
articles.body:
A couple who have waited a year to honeymoon in the Maldives are among tens of thousands of passengers stranded at UK airports.

Sam Stansfield said she and husband Dan should have left at 21:45 BST on Tuesday, but remain at London Stansted Airport, with Nats, the UK's air traffic services, blaming a technical glitch for widespread disruption.

The pair, from Lincoln, are now due to take off on Wednesday afternoon but will miss a connecting flight, further eating into their dream trip.

Sam, who said they spent the night "trying to sleep" on mats, added: "It's been horrendous. We are going all the way to the Maldives for about four days, but hey ho, it's better than Skegness."

Sam, who is travelling in a personalised hoodie bearing their wedding picture, said she monitored events at Heathrow and Gatwick on the BBC News website, before realising "how big it [the disruption] was".

She said there was "no room to move" at the airport earlier.

"They brought water around late at night and roll mats really late - at about 1am. It's horrible. We should be there [in the Maldives] now."

The couple only booked a relatively short trip due to not wanting to be away from their children for long and Sam's position as a childminder.

"I don't like to let people down," she said.

As the airport began to return to normal, the couple received an email informing them they are booked on a flight expected to depart at about 17:30 BST.

But the significant delay will mean they will miss a connecting flight from Abu Dabi, where they will have to wait a further six-and-a-half hours.

Martin Rolfe, the boss of Nats, has apologised for the disruption. He said there would be a full investigation, after the firm admitted resolving the issue had taken "longer than hoped".

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander has summoned Rolfe to a meeting on Wednesday to answer questions about the disruption and response.

She is expected to tell MPs that a cyber attack was "categorically" not the cause of the fault.

Sam added: "I'm hoping we can laugh about it at some point."

articles.summary: BHOPAL: Panic gripped Soumya Fortune Heritage colony in Misrod on Tuesday night when a Thar SUV allegedly went on a rampage, ramming into several park.
articles.body: BHOPAL: Panic gripped Soumya Fortune Heritage colony in Misrod on Tuesday night when a Thar SUV allegedly went on a rampage, ramming into several parked cars and SUVs, smashing through an exit gate and hitting more vehicles outside the residential complex.The driver also allegedly tried to drive towards women and children walking inside the colony, forcing them to flee to safety.No resident was seriously injured, though the colony guard sustained minor injuries and several residents had narrow escapes.Around a dozen cars and SUVs were damaged in the incident, while the SUV allegedly hit a stray animal as the driver fled the spot.The incident occurred around 9.30pm.Misrod police registered an FIR on the complaint of Kamal Singh Solanki, 55, a Soumya Fortune Heritage resident involved in the building material supply business.According to police, the SUV, bearing a Bhopal registration number, entered the colony at high speed and in a rash and negligent manner.It first rammed into Solanki's parked car while reversing, damaging both doors and the rear body.The SUV then reversed into another parked car belonging to Ashok Kumar Dubey, damaging its front.The impact pushed Dubey's car into a parked SUV belonging to Arvind Singh Raghuvanshi.The latter vehicle suffered damage to its front, police said. The driver allegedly continued his rampage, hitting two more cars parked inside the colony.Women, children flee as SUV heads towards themThe situation turned more alarming when the SUV allegedly headed towards women and children who were walking inside the colony.According to the complaint, the driver attempted to drive the vehicle towards them from behind, prompting the women and children to run for safety. They escaped without injuries.The SUV then headed towards the exit. Residents and security guards tried to stop the driver, but Gate No 2 had already been closed by a guard to prevent the vehicle from leaving.The driver allegedly rammed into the closed gate and forced his way out.A guard standing near the gate jumped into a nearby drain to save himself and sustained minor injuries, police said.More cars rammed outside colonyAfter breaking through the gate, the SUV allegedly rammed into a parked SUV belonging to Mahendra Kumar Dhurve outside the colony.The impact damaged it and pushed it into another parked sedan belonging to Mahendra Singh Rajput, damaging it.The SUV driver then fled from the spot. Police said several vehicles were damaged during the incident, while residents had narrow escapes.Driver often visited colony to meet female friendResidents later told police that the accused driver was known to frequently visit the colony to meet a female friend.Police are now trying to establish his identity and whereabouts based on information provided by the residents and CCTV footage from the colony and surrounding areas.During the investigation, police found that the SUV was registered in the name of an Obedullaganj-based owner.When contacted, the owner told police that he had given the SUV to someone else.Police are now tracing the person to whom the vehicle had been handed over and trying to identify and nab the man who was actually driving it when the rampage occurred.Around 150 residents reach police stationThe incident sparked anger among residents, with around 150 people from the colony approaching Misrod police station after the incident and demanding action against the driver.Police have registered a case under relevant provisions relating to rash and negligent driving and damage to property.Investigators are examining CCTV footage and questioning residents to establish the complete sequence of events and trace the accused.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhopal | Silver Rate in Bhopal | Bank Holidays in Bhopal | Public Holidays in Bhopal | Petrol Price in Bhopal | Diesel Price in Bhopal | CNG Price in Bhopal | LPG Price in BhopalStay updated with the latest Bhopal news. articles.title: A Colorado family has protected a 684-acre ranch that stayed in the same family for 90 years; its old cabin once served as a ranger and postmaster station
articles.summary: US News: A Colorado family has protected a 684-acre historic ranch after more than 90 years of family stewardship, ensuring that its agricultural landscape, wa.
articles.body: A Colorado family has protected a 684-acre historic ranch after more than 90 years of family stewardship, ensuring that its agricultural landscape, water resources, wildlife habitat and historic character can remain safeguarded for generations. Known as Ute Ranch, the property in western Montrose County has been placed under a permanent conservation easement through the Colorado Cattlemen’s Agricultural Land Trust. Owner Kathy Cooper donated the conservation easement rather than selling the ranch, allowing the land to remain privately owned while limiting future development. The property contains irrigated hay meadows, a reservoir, livestock infrastructure and historic buildings, while its past includes service as a U.S. Forest Service ranger station, postmaster’s station and seasonal cow camp. The ranch continues to support agriculture while providing habitat for wildlife.Colorado family protects 684-acre ranch after 90 yearsCooper’s family has cared for Ute Ranch for more than nine decades, with generations maintaining their connection to the property and its landscape. According to the Colorado Cattlemen’s Agricultural Land Trust, Cooper’s grandparents and parents worked hard for the property, leaving behind memories and a family heritage she wanted to preserve. Rather than allowing the ranch’s future to be shaped by development, Cooper chose to donate a conservation easement that will keep the land protected. She has described the ranch as her “go-to place” and “happy place”, reflecting its importance to her and her family. The decision means the property can remain a working ranch while carrying its conservation protections into the future.Historic ranch once served as a ranger and postmaster stationUte Ranch has a history that stretches beyond the Cooper family’s stewardship. The property once served as a U.S. Forest Service ranger station, a postmaster’s station and a seasonal cow camp, connecting it to the working history of the surrounding region. Several historic and agricultural structures remain on the property, including a barn, corrals, shed, bunkhouse and rustic cabin, along with remnants of the original homestead. The available conservation sources identify the ranch site as having served the ranger and postmaster functions, although they do not specifically establish that the surviving cabin itself served both roles. The historic structures therefore form part of a broader landscape preserving traces of the ranch’s earlier uses.684 acres remain a working landscapeThe conservation easement does not turn Ute Ranch into a closed nature preserve. The property remains an active agricultural landscape, with around 100 acres of irrigated hay meadows and a 40-acre reservoir. The reservoir provides water for cattle as well as wildlife, making the ranch’s water resources important to both agricultural production and the surrounding ecosystem. The property is also subject to a seasonal grazing arrangement with the neighbouring Galley family, allowing livestock production to continue. This combination of conservation and agriculture is central to the project, as the easement is designed to prevent incompatible development while retaining established working uses.Protected ranch provides habitat for wildlifeBeyond its value to ranching, Ute Ranch provides habitat for a range of wildlife. The Colorado Cattlemen’s Agricultural Land Trust identifies mule deer, elk and migratory birds among the species using the property. The ranch also forms part of a broader pattern of conserved private lands in western Montrose County. Protecting individual ranches can help maintain a larger connected landscape where agricultural fields, water sources and natural habitat remain together instead of being fragmented by development. The reservoir is particularly important because it provides water for both livestock and wildlife. The conservation easement therefore protects not only the acreage itself but also important ecological features within the property.Family donated conservation easement to protect the landThe protection of Ute Ranch was achieved through a conservation easement rather than an outright land purchase. Cooper continues to own the property, but the easement places permanent restrictions on development and other uses that could undermine its conservation values. Great Outdoors Colorado provided $40,000 through Keep It Colorado’s Transaction Cost Assistance Program to help with expenses associated with completing the conservation easement. The funding was support for the transaction and was not the purchase price of the ranch. The easement itself was donated by Cooper, making the decision a voluntary contribution of development rights to preserve the property’s agricultural and natural character.Ranch continues to connect children with its historyThe property also provides an opportunity for younger generations to experience the landscape. Great Outdoors Colorado says Cooper hosts an annual day camp for third-grade students from Naturita Elementary School. During visits to the ranch, children can learn about the local land and its history while developing a connection with the landscape. The educational use adds another dimension to the conservation project. Protecting Ute Ranch does not simply preserve acreage on a map. It helps retain a physical setting where stories about ranching, land stewardship and the region’s past can continue to be shared with future generations.Conservation easement protects the ranch for generationsThe easement includes two building envelopes covering about 7.5 acres, allowing existing structures and certain future activities to remain within designated areas while the larger ranch stays protected. The arrangement balances continued private ownership and agricultural use with permanent conservation restrictions. For Cooper’s family, the decision provides a way to carry forward the legacy of people who spent decades caring for the property without requiring future generations to make the same decision again. The conservation commitment becomes part of the land itself, allowing the 684 acres to continue supporting hay production, grazing, wildlife and family memories while remaining protected from development that could fundamentally change the landscape.Ute Ranch joins wider Colorado conservation effortUte Ranch is part of a broader effort to conserve privately owned agricultural and natural lands across Colorado. The Colorado Cattlemen’s Agricultural Land Trust was established in 1995 and says it has worked with more than 400 families to conserve more than 810,000 acres of Colorado farmland, ranchland, open space and wildlife habitat. The Ute Ranch project demonstrates how conservation easements can allow private landowners to retain ownership and continue ranching while permanently protecting important landscapes. In this case, the result is a combination of family history, agriculture, water and wildlife conservation on a property that has remained connected to one family for more than 90 years.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
